summary: Assistant-thread canonical binding columns (cinatra#1875, Epic #1873 W2, AC#4) — the operator-upgrade twin of the fresh-install bootstrap DDL (the two ADD COLUMN clauses in assistant-thread-schema.ts). A structured assistant thread gains its canonical binding {assistantPackage, instanceId?}: assistant_package (the registered assistant PACKAGE that drives the thread, package-keyed so the W1 registry reader's audience gate resolves the binding directly; NULL == an unbound implicit-@cinatra thread) and instance_id (the OPTIONAL project/site instance the binding is scoped to, carried into dispatch context; NULL when not instance-scoped). The binding is READ/WRITTEN at the same thread seam the W1 reader supports and is SEEDED by the W3 route (this wave lands persistence + store seam only). ADDITIVE + IDEMPOTENT + NON-DESTRUCTIVE: two nullable columns, both ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS so a second run or a ledger-faked fresh-bootstrap DB is a no-op and every pre-existing row is undisturbed (NULL == unbound). Rides the idempotent bootstrap DDL (assistantThreadSchemaQueries, same PR); this module carries the same ADD COLUMNs onto the operator upgrade path. Single all-or-nothing transaction; unqualified names resolve to the app schema on the runner's search_path. down() drops the two columns (true reverse; binding data lost by design as a structural addition, not a rename). SEQ IS PROVISIONAL + FLAGGED: shipped max on origin/main at cut time is core__0065 (#1915); #1935 holds core__0066 (legacy-bridge deletion) and test-delivery #1946 holds core__0067, so this slice claims the next genuinely-free sequence 0068 — a further concurrent sibling claiming 0068 first makes renumber-at-merge normal (rename-only, zero SQL diff). migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges (W2 routes as ONE unit once AC2 lands).
